DRR (Digitally Reconstructed Radiograph) geometry involves computing detector pixel positions in world coordinates and ray directions from a source to each pixel [S3, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly details the steps for computing DRR geometry. It states that detector pixel positions are calculated in world coordinates (using linspace, meshgrid, and stacking into a 3D array) and that ray directions are computed for each pixel by subtracting the source position from the detector pixel position (`ray_dir = detector_pixel - source`). This aligns perfectly with the claim.
